items.comment: The title is too broad and detailed, “a two-stage contract framework” sounds too specific and technical. We need to capture the most important and distinct aspect using the title for our work
“366 executions succeed, giving 91.50 % with a 95% Wilson interval of [88.36 %, 93.85 %].” This sentence should be removed from abstract
“an earlier marginal-interval disagreement was a statistical false alarm.” This sentence should be removed from abstract

The abstract should introduce the VQE briefly; then explain why we need the formal verification, and out of what points; we propose such 4-layer architecture and 2-stage framework for implementation; what’s the results we get and information and analysis to conclude; then what to do in the future and envision our work
Remove the 4 RQ component in section Introduction, but this section should be drafted around the need and importance to address these RQs, and make this section more intuitive and straightforward

Make the contributions in section Introduction bullet points. First, the 4-layer architecture of VQE formal verification, then the proposed specification and property to ensure the requirements, the 2-stage framework to evaluate the implementation, lastly the results we got

When you try to explain or introduce things or terms, just say it intuitively and expand with actual indication and meaning, don’t use negative statement to complement unless its necessary. Some meaningless examples such as “not a machine-checked refinement theorem”, “it is not a generator translating one specification into all three formalisms.” There are so many such sentences.
Don’t use so many Semicolon (;), avoid them as much as possible, only use them when needed

“The repository retains legacy “h2” names, but the operator has no documented molecular mapping and is not presented as a molecular-hydrogen Hamiltonian.” The how you get this H2, relabel the name and find the source
Cite papers where needed
Explain the why we choose such optimization method in section II-B
Rename the title of Section III to “Layered Verification Methodology”
Section IV-A, this whole subsection sounds awkward and confusing, we need to more explicitly and intuitively to introduce the experimental setup, configurations, selections, and boundaries etc.

There are only two evaluations we have done for the paper, one is the individual 4 layer verifications, another is the 2-stage framework evaluation. Don’t mingle them, but also don’t need to mention they are different or note them. Avoid using “final run”, “matched experiment”, “retained”, etc. just clearly state what are they
Rename title of  Section V-A to “Goals and Procedure”
There are too many tables,  replace the tables with figures when appropriate
The contract/specification/property can refer to the same meaning but have their specific characteristic, we need to clearly separate and use them appropriately across the whole paper
“frozen” in abstract and many other places in the paper sounds award and not intuitive, replace this
“50 updates” can be replaced by “50 iterations” or “50 evaluations”
Section “Shared Execution Model and Contract Library”, the term “contract” should be replaced by specification or property, if not, justify
“The shared execution view” in section II replace it with “The shared execution model”, stick with the term we have confirmed
In section II-B, the word  “canonical” should be replaced, also elsewhere in the paper, don’t use the term “canonical” it sounds awkward and indirect
Don’t use too many compound words unless its needed
Replace the term “evidence” across the whole paper when appropriate
Replace the term “seal” across the whole paper when appropriate
What does the term “subclaim” mean in Section V? replace this with a word that’s more intuitive and understandable
Rename the title of Section V-E to “Summary of Verification Results”, then analyze and summarize the verification process and results, add some insights and conclusions from the experiment
